goal: Replace ci:live-db-suites' R2 marker heuristic with AST extraction of EXECUTED SQL in live-DB suites, so run-time DDL is detected by what a suite runs rather than by whether it happens to name supabase/migrations, and bring all seven real DDL sites into compliance.
non_goals: Modifying scripts/ci/lib/sql-tag-scan.ts or SQL_TAG_NAMES — the four SQL vocabulary audits keep their exact current scope; this feature imports lineHasPragma and nothing else
Changing R1 (naming) detection or the LIVE_DB_MARKERS entry-point set — #573/#604 settled those and no evidence here contradicts them
Sanctioning bootstrap-by-ALTER as a pattern; assertSchemaReady remains the only supported way for a suite to depend on a migration
Adding a CONTEXT.md glossary section — this is test-infrastructure vocabulary, which by precedent (#573) lives in the audit header, the CLAUDE.md gotcha, and lab-notes
Applying, editing, or renumbering any supabase/migrations file; migration 083 already exists and is only ASSERTED here
Touching production code under src/lib/**, src/app/**/route.ts, or worker/** non-test paths
Fixing the #679 site in src/lib/reviews/__tests__/import-consent.integration.test.ts — it was already fixed on that branch and carries no DDL today
user_visible_behavior: pnpm ci:live-db-suites reports runtime-ddl for a live-DB suite that EXECUTES DDL through any tagged template or .unsafe() call, regardless of whether the file names supabase/migrations
pnpm ci:live-db-suites no longer depends on the string 'supabase/migrations' or '.unsafe(' appearing in a file to decide that DDL was applied
pnpm ci:live-db-suites reports NO finding for a DDL verb that appears only in a regex literal, a string assertion, a comment, or a non-executed constant
pnpm ci:live-db-suites reports runtime-ddl for a .unsafe() call whose argument is not a statically readable string (fail-closed), unless the file is allowlisted
A DDL line carrying a trailing `-- live-db-ddl-ignore: <reason>` pragma, or preceded by a comment-only pragma line, is exempt from runtime-ddl
pnpm ci:live-db-suites reports unlocked-ddl for an allowlisted DDL-probe suite that stops calling acquireLiveDbLock
pnpm ci:live-db-suites passes clean on the repository at HEAD after the three fixes and three exemptions land
invariants: R2 holds: no live-DB suite takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on a SHARED relation at run time, because that is the one deadlock ingredient (40P01) a suite controls
Every file exempted from R2 by allowlist must hold a cross-process lock — acquireLiveDbLock, or withMigration074ApplyLock for 074 only
Fail-closed: unresolvable SQL (a .unsafe() argument the audit cannot read statically) is treated as DDL, never as safe
The pragma exempts exactly one line; a code line carrying a trailing pragma never blankets the line below it (fail-open is the failure mode being avoided)
The audit's blast radius stays honest: any file reaching the live DB via LIVE_DB_MARKERS is scanned, and no tag-name allowlist narrows which of its statements are examined
scripts/ci/lib/sql-tag-scan.ts behavior is byte-identical after this change; the four vocabulary audits scan exactly what they scan today
A test that forces a transaction abort raises the failure in Postgres, not in JS — a JS throw does not poison a Postgres transaction and proves nothing about aborted state
The abort injection holds no schema, takes no ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, and strands nothing on the shared container whether its test passes, fails, or times out
edge_cases: sql() call-form tag: 770 of 1201 tagged templates in live-DB suites are tagged `sql()`, a CallExpression — a tag-name allowlist misses every one
db! NonNullExpression tag (73 uses) and one-off handles (sqlA(), observerSql(), dbC, boundedSql, recorder!, tierSql(), handle, seed, client, observer) — 21 distinct forms total
DDL verb inside a regex literal: migration-093/095/096/100/102 assert constraint text with /ALTER TABLE .../i and execute nothing
DDL verb inside expect().toContain('CREATE UNIQUE INDEX'): migration-091/093/096 read pg_indexes and assert on the returned indexdef
DDL verb inside a prose comment: migration-079 and migration-082 headers describe CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY without running it
DDL verb inside a non-executed string constant: migration-076 lines 115-142 hold an array of expected statements compared against migration text
.unsafe() with a non-literal argument: 13 sites, all readMigration0NNSql(), all in already-allowlisted suites 074/076/077/078/088 — fail-closed costs zero false positives today

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX on a TEMP table (migration-080:180,188) is textually identical to shared-table DDL; only the surrounding CREATE TEMP TABLE + pg_temp search_path shadowing makes it safe, so no statement-level analysis can resolve it — pragma required

CREATE TEMP TABLE itself (migration-080:80) also matches the DDL verb set; it gets a pragma too rather than a structural carve-out, so all three temp sites read uniformly and the reason sits where a reader needs it

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION auth.uid() inside a rolled-back tx under acquireLiveDbLock (outreach-render:355, migration-091:1207) is safe by lock + rollback, not by target — file allowlist so the lock stays enforced
migration-091 executes probe DDL but is NOT in MIGRATION_SHAPE_SUITES today, so its lock enrolment has never been checked by the audit
A vitest TIMEOUT skips a finally block — this is why the stranded tmp_block_import_topic_analytics CHECK survived and caused 14 spurious failures across three suites
Both bootstrap ALTERs are no-ops today (migration 083 is applied by pnpm test:db:setup) yet still take ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on job_outbox, the most contended relation in the live-DB set
The audit's own test file carries violating source as fixtures and must stay in NOT_LIVE_DB, or the tightened detector flags the tests that prove it works

scripts/ci/live-db-suites-audit.ts — the existing pure auditLiveDbSuite(file, text) signature, findings-array return, and NOT_LIVE_DB / MIGRATION_SHAPE_SUITES / OWN_APPLY_LOCK allowlist idiom

rollback_plan: No schema change and no deployed artifact: migration 083 already exists in both Supabase projects and is only ASSERTED here, never applied. Rollback is `git revert` of the squash-merge commit, which restores the previous detector and the previous test bodies together. No down migration, no flag flip, no ordering constraint. The one-way door to watch is the opposite direction: if the tightened detector proves too strict in CI, the escape is a per-line live-db-ddl-ignore pragma at the offending site, not reverting the detector.
observability: ci:live-db-suites is a CI gate, not a runtime path — the proof it works is the audit's own exit code plus its per-finding stderr lines (file [rule]: reason)

A regression in the detector's REACH shows up as `live-db-suites-audit: passed` on a tree that contains executed DDL; the repo-wide test ('every live-DB suite in the repository passes the tightened detector') is what makes that loud inside pnpm test rather than only in CI

A regression in the detector's PRECISION shows up as a runtime-ddl finding naming a file that only asserts about DDL text; the reason string carries file:line so the false positive is identifiable without re-running the scan

The failure this prevents has no signal of its own in prod — it appears as spurious cross-suite test failures on the shared container (40P01 deadlocks, or a stranded constraint blocking unrelated inserts). The #679 instance produced 14 such failures across three suites before anyone attributed them.
